summary: This OAuth app lets Composio-connected AI agents act on behalf of X end users (posting, reading, and optionally DMs). The biggest effort driver is that Composio has no managed X app, so you must create your own X developer account and app, and X's binding use-case approval and prepaid pay-per-use credits gate production access.

verdict.headline: Composio has no managed X app, so you need your own X developer account, an approved written use case, and prepaid credits before any user can connect.
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: Unknown. Depends on developer account approval, which has no documented timeline. Once approved, plan for about 2-4 hours of hands-on setup.
verdict.timeToProduction: Unknown. No official review SLA was found, and no community wait times were confirmed. Expect the use-case and account review to be the longest wait.
verdict.activeEffort: About 2-4 hours of hands-on work (estimate), excluding waiting.
verdict.approvalWait: Unknown. X reviews the use case and developer account, but no official SLA or measured wait time was found.

composio.guidance: You cannot start on Composio-managed auth for X. Create your own X app and a custom auth config in Composio before any user, including you, can connect. Once that is set up, you can test with your own account while the use-case approval is pending.

prerequisites.item: An X account that will own the developer app, with verified email (and phone if X asks)
prerequisites.why: Needed to sign up for a developer account. No business verification or legal entity requirement was found in the docs read.

prerequisites.item: A written use-case description covering agents acting for many end users
prerequisites.why: X reviews the use case, and it is binding. Any substantive change needs X's approval.

prerequisites.item: A funded prepaid credit balance in the Developer Console
prerequisites.why: There is no free tier. Pay-per-use credits are the reported model for new apps.

prerequisites.item: A Composio project where you can create a custom auth config
prerequisites.why: Composio requires the X client ID, client secret, and Application Bearer Token.

stages.title: Register the X developer account and app
stages.goal: You have a developer account with an approved use case and an OAuth 2.0 Web App with a client ID and secret.
stages.duration: 20-40 min hands-on, plus developer account approval wait (unknown)

steps.text: Sign in to X with the account that will own the app, then verify your email (and phone if prompted).
steps.detail: Phone verification may be required. The developer account support page is outdated on tier names, so ignore its 'Free, Basic, or Pro' wording.
Cover agents acting for many end users. Include posting, reading, and DMs if you request dm.read or dm.write. You must review and submit it yourself.

steps.text: Enter account name, location, and use-case details, accept the developer agreement, and confirm the verification email.
steps.detail: Paste the use-case text from the previous step. Any later change in purpose needs X's approval before you use the data for it.

steps.text: In console.x.com, go to Apps, click Create App, then open User authentication settings.
steps.detail: console.x.com loads publicly, but app management requires login. The legacy developer.x.com portal redirects to the x.com login page, so use console.x.com.

steps.text: Choose the Web App app type and enable OAuth 2.0.
steps.detail: Web App is a confidential client that issues a client secret. Native and single-page app types are public clients with no secret. OAuth 2.0 works only with API v2, and it must be switched on in the authentication settings.

steps.text: Save the Client ID and Client Secret, and copy the Application Bearer Token.
steps.detail: The bearer token is needed in Composio for search, post lookup, usage, compliance, and label-stream actions.

stages.title: Configure the callback, scopes, and Composio auth config
stages.goal: X and Composio share the same callback and scopes, and Composio has a working custom auth config for X.

steps.text: Copy the callback URL exactly as your Composio custom auth config shows it, and paste it into X's callback field.
steps.detail: The white-labeling doc gives https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/toolkits/auth/callback. Composio's KB says to use the exact callback its auth-config flow shows, not the legacy v1 one. X allows more than one callback, so registering both is a safe fallback.

steps.text: Generate the scope list for the agent's needs and confirm offline.access is included.
steps.detail: Scopes: tweet.read, tweet.write, tweet.moderate.write, users.email, users.read, follows.read, follows.write, offline.access, space.read, mute.read, mute.write, like.read, like.write, list.read, list.write, block.read, block.write, bookmark.read, bookmark.write, dm.read, dm.write, media.write, broadcast.read, broadcast.write. Without offline.access you get no refresh token, and access tokens last 2 hours.

steps.text: Create a custom auth config for X in Composio with the Client ID, Client Secret, and Application Bearer Token.
steps.detail: Without a custom auth config, connecting returns HTTP 400 ToolRouterV2_NoManagedAuth (code 4308) in a community report.

steps.text: Check that the bearer token belongs to the same app, and that the app's plan covers the endpoints you use.
steps.detail: A 401 on search or lookup endpoints means the bearer token is from a different app, or the plan doesn't cover that endpoint.

stages.title: Test with your own account
stages.goal: You connect your own X account, the token refreshes, and calls stay within rate limits.

steps.text: Connect your own X account through the Composio custom auth config.
steps.detail: If you see client-not-enrolled or App not linked to project, fix the X app or the Composio config, then recreate any EXPIRED connections.

steps.text: Confirm a refresh token was issued and that access tokens expire after about 2 hours.
steps.detail: Refresh is only available if offline.access was requested.

steps.text: Check request volume against the rate limits.
steps.detail: OAuth 2.0 allows 900 requests per 15 minutes per app for Tweet and user lookup. OAuth 1.0a allows 300.

stages.title: Get approved and go live for end users
stages.goal: X approves the use case and the account, credits are funded, and any restricted endpoints are removed from agent flows.
stages.duration: 30 min hands-on, plus use-case approval wait (unknown)

steps.text: Submit the use case for approval and wait for X's decision.
steps.detail: No official SLA was found. If your account is flagged during application, X asks you to request manual review.

steps.text: Confirm with X which scopes and endpoints are allowed on pay-per-use.
steps.detail: Reported restrictions include quote posts, likes, and follows. Not confirmed in official docs.

steps.text: Remove or disable any restricted endpoints from agent flows.
steps.detail: If X blocks likes, follows, or quote posts, agent tools that call them will fail.

steps.text: Load prepaid credits in the Developer Console and set per-user spend limits.
steps.detail: Every end-user action spends your credits. Reported prices are about $0.015 per post created, $0.20 per post with a link, and $0.005 per post read. Verify on the official pricing page.

steps.text: Monitor compliance and usage, and keep the use case current.
steps.detail: X can suspend or revoke access for usage beyond the approved scope or for policy violations.

blockers.title: Composio has no managed X app
blockers.symptom: Connecting without a custom auth config returns HTTP 400 ToolRouterV2_NoManagedAuth (code 4308): 'Composio does not manage auth for toolkit twitter'.
blockers.workaround: Create your own X Web App and a custom auth config in Composio with the client ID, secret, and bearer token.

blockers.title: Callback URL mismatch
blockers.symptom: The exact error text was not documented. Expect the authorization redirect to fail or the connection to not complete.
blockers.workaround: Copy the callback exactly from your Composio auth config. Register both the v3.1 and v1 URLs if you're unsure which one your flow uses.

blockers.title: Bearer token returns 401 on search or lookup
blockers.symptom: 401 Unauthorized on search, post lookup, usage, compliance, or label-stream actions.
blockers.workaround: Confirm the bearer token comes from the same app, and that the app's plan covers the endpoint.

blockers.title: App not linked to project or client-not-enrolled
blockers.symptom: Errors client-not-enrolled or App not linked to project.
blockers.workaround: Fix the X app or the Composio config, then recreate any EXPIRED connections.

blockers.title: Account flagged during developer application
blockers.symptom: Your developer account application is flagged and you're asked to request manual review.
blockers.workaround: Request manual review through X's support channel. No wait times were found.

blockers.title: Use case rejected or access suspended
blockers.symptom: Access is revoked or suspended for going beyond the approved use case or for policy violations.
blockers.workaround: Keep the use case current. Submit substantive changes for X's approval before you use data for the new purpose.

blockers.title: Restricted endpoints fail under pay-per-use
blockers.symptom: Likes, follows, or quote-post calls fail even though the scope is granted.
blockers.workaround: Confirm with X which endpoints work on your plan. Remove restricted actions from agent flows.

blockers.title: Unexpected credit spend
blockers.symptom: Credits drain as end users take actions, since there is no free tier.
blockers.workaround: Fund credits deliberately, set per-user limits, and monitor usage in the Developer Console.

nuances.text: The Developer Console at console.x.com loads publicly, and the legacy developer.x.com portal redirects to login. Use console.x.com.
A probe of the authorize endpoint returned a login page for a fake client ID. That shows the endpoint is live, but it does not validate your client or callback.
X has no OpenID Connect discovery document, so endpoints must be configured by hand.
twitter.com/i/oauth2/authorize redirected to x.com in a probe, but a community report says it returned 404 in April 2026. Use x.com.
The developer account support page still lists Free, Basic, and Pro tiers. Treat it as outdated.
No user cap or test-mode token expiry was found in the docs, but access tokens last 2 hours unless you use offline.access.

claims.statement: Composio's directory lists Twitter (slug twitter) as not managed, meaning it has no Composio-managed OAuth app.
claims.note: Retrieved via the lookup tool, not a direct page read in the dossier. [Checker: not found in the cited source. The managed-auth page explains the concept of Composio-managed OAuth apps but does not list toolkits or a Twitter/slug 'twitter' entry; the directory is loaded dynamically ('Loading toolkits...'), and the page says to check via the API or toolkit page.]

claims.statement: Composio's knowledge base says managed Twitter credentials were removed in February 2026. A custom X developer app and a custom auth config are required.
claims.note: The exact wording of the Feb 12 2026 changelog was not read. [Checker: confirmed in source. The Composio KB says 'Composio-managed credentials are not available for the Twitter toolkit... since managed Twitter credentials were removed in February 2026,' and requires a customer-owned OAuth app plus a custom auth config.]

claims.statement: Connecting without a custom auth config returns HTTP 400 ToolRouterV2_NoManagedAuth (code 4308): 'Composio does not manage auth for toolkit twitter'.

sources.title: Connecting Twitter fails because Composio has no managed auth (issue 2415)

claims.note: A single community report. Reported one day before the research date.

claims.statement: The Composio auth config needs the app's Application Bearer Token in addition to the client ID and secret. Search, post lookup, usage, compliance, and label-stream actions use it. A 401 on these means the bearer token is from a different app or the plan doesn't cover the endpoint.
claims.note: [Checker: confirmed in source. The KB says search/counts, post lookup by IDs, post usage, label-stream and compliance-job actions 'read the Application Bearer Token from the Twitter auth config,' and that if these return 401, verify the bearer token comes from the same X Developer App and that the app's plan allows the endpoint.]

claims.statement: The errors client-not-enrolled and App not linked to project mean the X app isn't linked to a project or its config is stale. Fix the app, then recreate any EXPIRED connections.
claims.note: [Checker: confirmed in source. The KB says 'client-not-enrolled' and 'App not linked to project' usually mean the app is not connected to a project or the OAuth configuration is stale; it advises fixing the app and, if the connection is EXPIRED, recreating it.]

claims.statement: Developer account signup requires logging in to X, verifying email (phone may also be needed), entering account name, location, and use-case details, accepting the developer agreement, and confirming the verification email.
claims.note: The same page's tier wording is outdated. [Checker: confirmed in source. The X support page lists logging in and verifying email ('phone number verification... may be needed'), entering developer account name, location and use case details, accepting the developer agreement, and checking email for 'Verify your X Developer Account.']

claims.statement: The Composio walkthrough path is console.x.com, then Apps, then Create App, then User authentication settings, then OAuth 2.0. Choose the app type, add the callback, and save the client ID and secret.

claims.statement: X reviews proposed uses. The written use case is binding, and any substantive change needs X's approval before you use data for the new purpose. Usage beyond the allowed scope needs an Enterprise plan. X can suspend or revoke access.
